## Xi Jinping in 2024: `1B.2` nuclear-rhetoric review

Best read: **Xi/China’s official 2024 nuclear rhetoric was mostly restrained and responsibility-coded**. It repeatedly emphasized no-first-use, “nuclear war must not be fought,” and arms-control language. I found **no reliable 2024 source showing Xi personally used reckless nuclear threats or apocalyptic language**. The main counterweight is **behavioral/contextual**: China’s nuclear buildup and coercive military signaling weaken the credibility of the rhetoric, but they are not direct examples of reckless nuclear rhetoric.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports responsible rhetoric | [No-first-use of Nuclear Weapons Initiative](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202407/t20240723_11458632.html | Official Chinese nuclear policy paper says Xi “re-affirmed” that nuclear weapons cannot be used and nuclear war must not be fought, and promotes mutual no-first-use. This is direct evidence for restrained nuclear rhetoric. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| Supports responsible rhetoric | [Security Assurances](https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng./xw/wjbxw/202407/t20240723_11458631.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-23 | https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng./xw/wjbxw/202407/t20240723_11458631.html | China called for unconditional negative security assurances, no first use, no threat of use against non-nuclear states, and reduced nuclear-alert practices. The language is cautionary and anti-escalatory, not apocalyptic. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| Supports responsible rhetoric | [China firmly against US, Japan's false narrative on China's nuclear policy](https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2024-04/12/content_117120636.htm) | Xinhua / State Council Information Office | 2024-04-12 | https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2024-04/12/content_117120636.htm | Beijing rejected claims that China’s nuclear buildup was destabilizing, repeated no-first-use language, and said China keeps capabilities at the minimum required for national security. Again, the rhetoric is defensive and non-catastrophic. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| Cautions against over-crediting rhetoric | [Role of nuclear weapons grows as geopolitical relations deteriorate - new SIPRI Yearbook out now](https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now) | SIPRI | 2024-06-17 | https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2024/role-nuclear-weapons-grows-geopolitical-relations-deteriorate-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now | SIPRI reported China’s arsenal rising from 410 warheads in Jan. 2023 to 500 in Jan. 2024 and said some warheads may be deployed on missiles in peacetime. This is not rhetoric, but it undercuts the credibility of purely responsible nuclear messaging. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| Cautions against over-crediting rhetoric | [Senior Defense Official Briefs on 2024 China Military Power Report](https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/) | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-12-18 | https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4009708/senior-defense-official-briefs-on-2024-china-military-power-report/ | DoD said China surpassed 600 operational nuclear warheads by mid-2024 and continued a rapid buildup. That is a strong counter-context to “responsible rhetoric,” though still not direct reckless rhetoric. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| Indirect caution | [PLA conducts joint military drills surrounding Taiwan Island](https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html) | PRC Ministry of National Defense / Xinhua | 2024-05-23 | https://eng.mod.gov.cn/xb/News_213114/TopStories/16310652.html | The PLA announced combat-readiness patrols and “stern warning” drills around Taiwan. This is coercive signaling, not nuclear rhetoric, but it adds to a broader brinkmanship context. | `1B.2`, `6A` |

### Synthesis

- **Direct evidence for responsible nuclear rhetoric is strong.**
- **Direct evidence of reckless nuclear rhetoric by Xi in 2024 is weak or absent in the material I found.**
- **The main counterevidence is contextual, not rhetorical**: nuclear buildup and military coercion make the restraint language less convincing, but they do not prove reckless nuclear threats.

### Search gap

I did **not** find a credible 2024 source showing Xi personally used:
- explicit nuclear threats,
- apocalyptic or “end of the world” language,
- public brinkmanship around nuclear use,
- or normalization of nuclear use.
